citation.title: Integrity Checklist for National Delegations to COP
citation.venue_or_publisher: Transparency International (published 2025-08-28 per the extracted file)

question: Not a research study. It sets out what national delegations to the UNFCCC COP should do to show transparency, accountability and integrity in their make-up and conduct, and to prevent undue influence by fossil fuel and other high-polluting industries.

definitions.term: high-polluting industries (as used for delegates to avoid)
definitions.definition: Industries, besides fossil fuel companies, whose core business is incompatible with the goals of the Paris Agreement. No list of sectors or test is given.
definitions.quote: high polluting industries whose core business is incompatible with the goals of the Paris Agreement

definitions.term: affiliation with fossil fuel and other high-polluting industries (what delegates should disclose)
definitions.definition: Affiliations can be with private or state-owned entities and include ownership, board or governance seats, leadership positions, consultancy contracts and unpaid advisory roles; the list is open (not limited to these).
definitions.quote: including (but not limited to) shareholders/owners, members of board of other supervisory/governance/ body; leadership positions; consultancy contracts and unpaid adviserships

definitions.term: who is covered (national delegation and party overflow)
definitions.definition: The checklist covers all participants in national delegations and those under party overflow. Party overflow is not defined beyond the reference to badges.
definitions.quote: The checklist applies to all participants in national delegations and under party overflow.

proxies.concept: fossil fuel / high-polluting industry link of a delegate
proxies.indicator: Any of the affiliation types listed for disclosure (ownership, board or governance seat, leadership position, consultancy contract, unpaid advisership), with private or state-owned entities; also current and former affiliations in the code of conduct declaration.
proxies.quote: Declaring all relevant current and former affiliations with fossil fuel and other high polluting industries.

recommendations.point: Do not appoint delegates affiliated with fossil fuel companies and other high-polluting industries; the authors say their presence delegitimises delegations and raises concerns about undue influence.
recommendations.quote: Their presence delegitimises National Delegations and raises concerns on the undue influence of high polluters contrary to the goals of the Paris Agreement and the purpose of COPs.

recommendations.point: Publish a full, up-to-date list of delegates and party overflow badge holders well ahead of COP.
recommendations.quote: publish a full, up-to-date list of all delegates in national delegation, and participants holding “party overflow badges.”

recommendations.point: Set conflict of interest rules to keep people with ties to major polluting industries from influencing negotiations against climate ambition.
recommendations.quote: polluting industries from influencing negotiations in ways that undermine climate ambition.

recommendations.point: Require a signed code of conduct, with declared affiliations and procedures for breaches including removal from delegations.
recommendations.quote: Declaring all relevant current and former affiliations with fossil fuel and other high polluting industries.

limitations.point: The extracted file holds the whole document: one page, about 436 words. Nothing is missing, but the document is short and gives no data.
The document is a normative checklist. It reports no data, no method, no counts and no findings, so it gives no figure for business or fossil-fuel presence in delegations.

It does not define 'business' or 'private sector' for delegates, and does not set out how fossil-fuel or high-polluting links should be identified, which sectors count, or any threshold. It names no reference list.

The extracted text has some broken sentences (checkbox text is split across lines and the wording of the disclosure item is garbled, for example 'members of board of other supervisory/governance/ body'). Quotes keep the extracted wording exactly.

The title field of the extracted file runs into the first sentence of the text; the title used here is the heading on page 1. The author name and publication date come from the file's metadata, not the page text.
No instructions addressed to a reader or an AI were found in the text.

pages_read: Whole extracted text: page 1 of 1 (the PDF has one page), all 436 words. Nothing is missing.
